predeclared.note: Saved before any R3_risk number was computed. The REPORT text is stored in results.json (section report_md) and in the structured answer: this subagent is instructed not to write report .md files.
predeclared.book: Frozen PROD book (PREREG_R3): weekly step 5, 4 staggered sleeves, top-20 slot sizing, 20d time exit, elig_base (liq2), 50 bps central / 80 bps stress, phase-averaged over the 5 weekly entry phases.

item1_drawdowns.episode_definition: peak (new equity high) -> trough (min before recovery) -> recovery (first close >= peak); non-overlapping episodes ranked by depth; top 5
item1_drawdowns.monthly: calendar-month compounded returns; mean/median/sd/percentiles/% positive; % months beating random, EW, Nifty 500

list.X80: 80% invested at every sleeve rebalance, 20% in Nifty 1D Rate Index
list.X60: 60% invested at every sleeve rebalance, 40% in Nifty 1D Rate Index
list.G50: breadth50 (signal-date close) < 0.5 -> that sleeve invests 50% (rest Nifty 1D Rate) until its next rebalance; else 100%

item2_exposure_policies.pre_note: No PROD scores exist before 2023 (walk-forward); PRE uses the EW-universe book only.
stats: paired diff vs X100 + NW t (lag 20)
item2_exposure_policies.adoption: PREREG rule applied to G50 (DEV paired NW t >= 2 and maxDD not worse by > 3 pp). X80/X60 are risk-budget dials, reported as a menu, not alpha add-ons.

item3_expectations.method: circular block bootstrap, blocks {20, 40 (primary), 60} trading days, 10,000 paths of 504 days
item3_expectations.source: phase-averaged daily excess (PROD book - 5-seed random) on DEV (primary); contiguous 2023-01..2026-10 as sensitivity
item3_expectations.shift: series demeaned then shifted to +5%/yr (planning) and to 0%/yr (dead book)
item3_expectations.excess_definition: sum of daily excess returns over the window (arithmetic)
outputs: absolute return = EW universe daily + shifted excess (joint blocks; EW at its historical source-window mean)

singles.K2: rolling 3-month (63 signal dates) mean matured rank IC < 0.02; IC of signal date t is known at t+20, so at check date T the window is signal dates (T-20-62 .. T-20)

extra_variants_justified_in_advance.C1_review: K1 OR K2 OR K3 (a review trigger: maximise detection, accept false alarms)
extra_variants_justified_in_advance.C2_kill: K3 AND K2 at the same weekly check (money AND signal both failing; protects against monetisation luck such as 2026 where IC was intact but excess ~0)
extra_variants_justified_in_advance.C3_kill_fast: K1 AND K2 at the same weekly check (faster version of C2)

item4_kill_rules.checks: weekly (every 5 trading days) over the first 24 months (504 days) of live trading; a rule can fire only once its window is full

hypotheses.H1a: +5%/yr excess, IC mean = PROD DEV IC (IC intact, monetisation weaker, as in 2026)
hypotheses.H1b: +5%/yr excess, IC mean = PROD DEV IC x (0.05 / PROD DEV excess) (IC proportional to excess)

resampling: joint circular block bootstrap of daily (excess, IC) pairs on DEV, blocks 20/40/60 (dependence-preserving)

persistence-matched null books: random scores = sqrt(w)*entity constant + sqrt(1-w)*AR(1)(rho) fitted to PROD's own rank autocorrelation (lags 5, 250); each null book's own phase-averaged excess and IC series evaluated in rolling 24-month windows (H0 directly; H1 by adding the drift)
item4_kill_rules.iid_reference: an iid daily bootstrap is shown ONLY to illustrate the bias of ignoring dependence; never used to calibrate
item4_kill_rules.historical: the rules' behaviour on the actual 2023-2026 PROD book is reported (DEV and 2026)
dashboard: top-20 relative hit rate (label pct > 0.5) and absolute hit (net > 0)
turnover (top-20 overlap with the same sleeve's previous list; round trips/yr)
slippage vs open (backtest fills at the official open; budget from the 50 bps cost model)

predeclared.variants_count_plan: exposure 4 policies (X100 baseline + 3) x books; kill rules 3 singles + 3 extras; bootstrap block lengths are sensitivity settings, not selections

notes: Nifty 500 is a price index (no dividends, ~1.2%/yr); book/EW/random use CA-adjusted prices incl. dividends.
First calendar month is partial and the 4 sleeves ramp up over the first 15 trading days; it is excluded from the monthly statistics when the series starts after the 7th.

Exposure set at each sleeve's rebalance (signal close); idle share earns the Nifty 1D Rate Index from that close. X100 = frozen baseline (idle cash 0%, identical to L.Sim). X100_cash is a diagnostic (idle cash at 1D rate), not a policy.
PRE (2021-09..2022-12) exists only for the EW-universe book: no PROD scores before 2023.
Sharpe uses rf = 0 (as C.stats_from_daily); Calmar = CAGR / |maxDD| over the period.

html_tables.title: The five worst falls of the strategy (Jan-2023 to Oct-2026) and what the market did over the same days
html_tables.note: Strategy = frozen PROD book (top-20, weekly, 20-day holds, 50 bps costs), averaged over the 5 weekday entry phases. The worst fall (Dec-2024 to Mar-2025) was a broad small/mid-cap sell-off: random picks and the equal-weight universe fell as much; the model did not cause it and could not avoid it. Nifty 500 is a price index (no dividends).

html_tables.title: Monthly returns, 2023-01 to 2026-09 (45 months)
html_tables.note: Monthly compounded returns of the daily book. The strategy swings as much as the small/mid-cap universe (about 6% a month), roughly 1.5x the Nifty 500.

html_tables.title: How often the strategy beat the alternatives, month by month
html_tables.note: Even in the strong development years the strategy lost to random picks in about 3 months out of 10; in 2026 it beat random in fewer than half of the months.

html_tables.title: Months when the market fell, was flat, or rose
html_tables.note: The strategy is a fully invested long book of mostly mid/small caps: in falling months it falls more than the Nifty 500. Its edge shows up mainly in flat and rising months.

html_tables.title: Exposure choices for the strategy book (50 bps costs)
html_tables.note: Cash earns the Nifty 1D Rate. Gain vs 100% = annualised daily difference with a Newey-West t (lag 20). No policy passes the pre-registered adoption rule (needs t >= 2): the breadth governor cut the worst fall by about 10 points in 2023-2025 but gave up return overall; it gained 12.2% during the single Dec-2024 to Mar-2025 sell-off and lost -18.8% the rest of the time. 'Sharpe vs cash' subtracts the cash rate; plain Sharpe (rf = 0) flatters cash-heavy choices.

html_tables.title: Exposure choices tested on the all-stock equal-weight book, including 2021-22
html_tables.note: No model scores exist before 2023 (walk-forward), so the 2021-22 test uses the equal-weight universe book. In the choppy 2022 market the breadth governor switched ~10 times a year and did worse than staying invested.

html_tables.title: What to expect: the strategy's lead over random picks after 6, 12 and 24 months
html_tables.note: Block bootstrap (40-day blocks, 10,000 paths) of the 2023-2025 daily excess, re-centred on the planning edge (+5%/yr) or on zero. Even with a real +5% edge, about 1 year in 4 ends behind random picks; a dead strategy looks like a +5% one about 1 year in 4.

html_tables.title: Sensitivity of the expectations to how the history is resampled
columns: P(behind random in a year | +5% edge)
P(at least one losing year in two | +5% edge)
P(dead strategy shows > +5% in a year)
html_tables.note: Longer blocks keep more of the day-to-day persistence and widen the ranges; treating days as independent understates the risk of a bad year. Primary = 40-day blocks.

html_tables.title: What to expect in rupees: total return ranges (market + strategy edge)
html_tables.note: Total return = equal-weight universe daily return + the re-centred edge, resampled together in 40-day blocks. The market part keeps its 2023-2025 average (equal-weight book 11.2%/yr after costs), which may be optimistic. Market risk dominates: the edge changes the middle, not the width.

html_tables.title: Kill and review rules: false alarms vs detection over the first 24 months of live trading
columns: False alarm, good strategy (+5%, IC intact)
html_tables.note: Joint 40-day block bootstrap of the daily (lead over random, IC) history 2023-2025, re-centred: good = +5%/yr with IC 0.067 (as observed), pessimistic good = +5%/yr with IC 0.022 (IC scaled down with the edge), dead = 0%/yr and IC 0. IC of a signal date is known 20 trading days later. Null books = 100 random scores with the same day-to-day persistence as the model (rolling 24-month windows). Recommended: C2 as the kill rule; K1 and K2 as review triggers.

html_tables.title: How the rules would have behaved on our own backtest (weekly checks to 2026-09-30)
html_tables.note: Only the 6-month review rule fired (Jan-2024), a false alarm: the 12-month lead never fell below 6.6% over the whole backtest. At the last check the 6-month lead was -1.6%, the 12-month lead 7.8% and the 3-month IC 0.080: no rule active.

html_tables.title: Weekly monitoring dashboard: what normal looked like in 2023-2025 and what 2026 showed
rows: Signal quality (rank IC of the score vs realised 20-day relative return)
Review if the 13-week average < 0.02 (K2); kill only with C2
Top-20 relative hit rate (share of picks beating the median stock after neutralisation)
Top-20 absolute hit rate (share of picks with net 20-day return > 0)
Top-20 return minus universe average (20-day, before costs)
Avoid list (bottom 30%) return minus universe average (20-day)
Review if the 13-week average turns positive
Turnover: share of this week's top-20 also picked 4 weeks ago (same sleeve)
By construction each weekly rebalance sells the expiring 20 and buys 20 new; if the overlap stays above 0.30 (2023-25 weekly 90th pct was 0.19) check that the score file is updating
Slippage vs the official open (bps per side)
Budget 13.8 bps/side beyond statutory (~22.3 bps round trip) inside the 50 bps all-in cost; review above it, stop adding money above 28.9 (= 80 bps stress, which cost 4.7%/yr of return in 2023-2025)
html_tables.note: All values are fractions (0.067 = 6.7%). 2026 values are reported, never used to set thresholds. In 2026 the signal quality and relative hit rate stayed normal while the top-20's raw return lead nearly vanished: the information survived but did not turn into money. A likely (not verified here) cause is the book's factor tilts; round 2 found it leans away from momentum, which led in 2026.

drawdown_weekly.note: How far each portfolio was below its previous high, weekly (0 = at a new high). The strategy's worst fall (-27%, early 2025) matched random picks; it recovered to its peak in Jul-2026.

equity_monthly.note: Growth of 1 rupee, Jan-2023 to Oct-2026, 50 bps costs, averaged over the 5 weekday entry phases.

monthly_return_histogram.note: Number of months in each monthly-return bucket (end buckets include the tails).

exposure_policies.note: Holding cash lowers both the return and the worst fall almost one-for-one; none of these is a free lunch.

expected_12m_lead.note: Range of the 12-month lead over random picks. The two ranges overlap heavily: one year of results cannot tell a good strategy from a dead one.

kill_rule_tradeoff.note: A good rule has a short first bar and a tall second bar. Money-only rules fire too often on a good strategy; combining money with signal quality (C2) keeps detection and cuts false alarms.

rules_history_lead.note: Rolling lead of the strategy over random picks on our own backtest (weekly).

rules_history_ic.note: Signal quality never fell below the review line, including 2026.

item1_excess_by_year_sum.note: sums of daily (book - random) on the contiguous phase-averaged book; 2026 to Oct-14

report_md:
# R3_risk — exposure, drawdowns, expectations, monitoring and kill rules

Frozen PROD book (PREREG_R3): weekly, 4 staggered sleeves, top-20, 20-day time exit, elig_base (liq2), 50 bps
(80 bps stress), phase-averaged over the 5 weekly entry phases. DEV = 2023-2025 (selection), 2026 = reported only.
All numbers below are in results/R3_risk/results.json. Pre-declaration (incl. the 3 extra kill-rule combos) was
saved in results.json before any number was computed (section `predeclared`).

## 1. Drawdown anatomy (contiguous 2023-01 -> 2026-10, phase-averaged, 50 bps)
* Book: CAGR 24.6%, excess vs random 12.8%/yr (NW t 3.79),
  maxDD -26.8%; random top-20 maxDD -33.3%, EW universe
  -34.6%, Nifty 500 (price) -18.8%.
* Worst episode: peak 2024-12-16 -> trough 2025-03-03 (-26.8%, 54 trading days), back to peak
  2026-07-10 (387 trading days). Same window: random -26.1%, EW
  -26.5%, Nifty 500 -14.8%. Boring explanation confirmed: a market-wide
  small/mid-cap sell-off, not a model failure (book minus random -0.8%).
* 5th episode is still open: peak 2026-08-03, -6.4% so far, -3.8% vs random.
* Monthly (45 months): mean 2.0%, sd 6.2%,
  worst -13.9%; beat random in 69.4% of DEV months and
  44.4% of 2026 months. In Nifty-500 months below -3% the book averaged
  -8.1% vs Nifty -6.4%:
  a full-beta mid/small-cap long book with no downside protection.
* Excess by year (sum of daily excess, contiguous): 2023 8.3%, 2024 25.9%, 2025 11.9%,
  2026 YTD 1.3%.

## 2. Exposure policies (pre-declared X100 / X80 / X60 / G50)
* Validation: own sleeve simulator = L.Sim bit-exact (max abs daily diff 0.0).
* PROD DEV: X100 CAGR 30.3% / maxDD -26.8%; X80 25.6% /
  -21.7%; X60 20.8% / -16.3%; G50 28.4% /
  -16.6% (risk-off on 39.3% of signals,
  6.9 switches/yr).
* 2026: X100 10.2% / -17.5%; G50 7.7% /
  -9.4%. PRE 2021-09..2022-12 (EW book only, no PROD scores before 2023): X100
  -2.5% / -25.9%; G50 -5.3% / -23.7%
  with 10.1 switches/yr (whipsaw).
* Adoption rule: G50 DEV gain -2.3%/yr, NW t -0.62 -> NOT adopted (needs t >= 2).
  Its maxDD benefit is one episode: +12.2% inside 2024-12-16..2025-03-03,
  -18.8% over the rest of DEV.
* Static cash is a risk dial, not alpha: Sharpe in excess of cash DEV X100 1.15, X80 1.15,
  X60 1.16 (the rf=0 Sharpe rise 1.48 -> 1.71 is the cash yield).

## 3. Expectations (circular block bootstrap of DEV daily excess, 40-day blocks primary, 10,000 paths)
* +5%/yr plan: 12-month excess p5 -6.7%, median 5.0%, p95
  16.6%; P(negative excess year) 24.2% (20-day blocks
  22.6%, 60-day 25.9%); P(at least one negative year in two)
  42.0%; 24-month excess median 10.1%, P(<0)
  16.3%.
* Dead book (0%): P(12-month excess > +5%) 24.0% -> one year cannot separate skill from luck.
* Absolute (EW universe + excess, EW at its DEV mean, EW CAGR 11.2%): +5% plan 12-month p5 -19.6%,
  median 18.1%, p95 60.4%, P(loss) 22.3%;
  2-year worst fall median -21.0%, P(worse than -20%) 54.5%,
  P(worse than -30%) 18.3%.
* Daily excess autocorrelation is small (lag 20: 0.074), so blocks widen the 12-month spread only modestly
  (sd 6.4% iid -> 7.0% 40-day blocks). Dependence matters far more
  for the IC (overlapping 20-day labels): see section 4.

## 4. Kill / review rules (weekly checks over the first 24 months; joint (excess, IC) block bootstrap on DEV)
H1a = +5%/yr with IC 0.067 (as observed), H1b = +5%/yr with IC 0.022 (IC scaled with the edge),
H0 = 0%/yr and IC 0. IC of signal date t is known at t+20. 40-day blocks (range over 20/60-day blocks in brackets).
| rule | false alarm H1a | false alarm H1b | detect H0 24m | median days |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| K1 | 51.6% (43.8%-55.6%) | 51.6% | 77.4% | 220.0 |
| K2 | 23.6% (16.7%-23.6%) | 99.9% | 100.0% | 85.0 |
| K3 | 61.3% (60.8%-62.1%) | 61.3% | 86.7% | 255.0 |
| C1_review | 71.6% (69.3%-72.2%) | 99.9% | 100.0% | 85.0 |
| C2_kill | 7.6% (4.7%-7.6%) | 53.1% | 85.5% | 255.0 |
| C3_kill_fast | 6.9% (3.2%-6.9%) | 44.7% | 76.2% | 225.0 |

* K1 = 6m excess < -5%; K2 = 3m mean matured IC < 0.02; K3 = 12m excess < 0; C1 = any; C2 = K3 AND K2; C3 = K1 AND K2.
* iid resampling (reference only, NOT used) would put K2's H1a false alarm at 0.0% vs
  23.6% with 40-day blocks: ignoring the IC's persistence badly understates false alarms.
* Persistence-matched null books (100 AR(1)+entity scores fitted to PROD's rank autocorrelation, w 0.214, rho 0.924):
  C2 detection 88.4%, false alarm H1a 0.0%. Null books have lower
  tracking error (4.9% vs model 6.6%) and IC noise
  (0.030 vs 0.046), so their false alarms are optimistic; the bootstrap is primary.
* On our own backtest only K1 ever fired (2024-01-10, 2024-01-17; false alarm: 12m excess never below
  6.6%); the 3m IC minimum was 0.024 (2023-11-06).
  Last check 2026-09-30: 6m -1.6%, 12m 7.8%, IC 0.080 -> no rule active.
  Watch-out: the 12m figure still contains 2025-Q4 (6.2%); 2026 YTD excess is only 1.3%, so K3 can trigger a review in early 2027.

Recommended rule set: REVIEW (investigate, no automatic action) when any of K1, K2, K3 fires — expect at least one review
in 24 months even for a good book (71.6%). KILL (stop new entries, let sleeves run off)
when C2 fires: 7.6% false alarm vs 85.5% detection, typically ~255
trading days after a book dies. The K2 review is the early warning: a dead signal trips it at the first possible check
(85 trading days). If the true IC of a good book were only ~0.022 (H1b), C2's
false alarm would be 53.1%: re-calibrate if the 13-week IC runs below its DEV 10th percentile
(0.038) while excess stays positive.

## 5. Weekly dashboard (DEV normal ranges; 2026 reported)
* Rank IC: DEV 0.067 (weekly p10 0.002, p90 0.118); 2026 0.063.
* Top-20 relative hit (label pct > 0.5): DEV 0.553, 2026 0.567; absolute hit (net > 0):
  DEV 0.551, 2026 0.498.
* Top-20 raw 20d return minus universe: DEV 1.3%, 2026 0.1%;
  avoid tail (bottom 30%) minus universe: DEV -0.6%, 2026 -0.3%.
  2026 = signal intact, monetisation gone (consistent with factor tilts; not verified here).
* Turnover: top-20 overlap with the same sleeve 4 weeks earlier DEV 0.085, 2026 0.114
  (every pick is a full round trip under the frozen time exit).
* Slippage vs open: budget 13.85 bps/side beyond ~22.3 bps statutory (50 bps all-in);
  stress 28.85 bps/side (80 bps), which cost 4.7%/yr of DEV CAGR.

## Pros
* Drawdowns are market drawdowns: worst episode matched random/EW; overall maxDD shallower than random and EW over 2023-2026.
* A money-AND-signal kill rule (C2) separates good from dead books far better than money-only rules.
* The IC is a fast, objective diagnostic (matures in 20 days) and stayed normal through 2026.
* Static exposure is a clean risk dial (Sharpe vs cash unchanged), letting the client pick risk without touching the edge.
## Cons
* No exposure policy passes the adoption rule; the breadth governor's benefit is one episode and it whipsawed in 2022.
* One year cannot tell a +5% book from a dead one; money-only rules give 52-61% false alarms in 24 months.
* IC-based rules assume a good book keeps IC near its DEV level; if IC scales down with the edge, C2's false alarm jumps.
* Full-beta mid/small-cap book: ~1 in 4.5 chance of a losing 12 months even with the planned edge; typical 2-year worst fall ~-21%.
## Caveats
* PROD exists only 2023+ (walk-forward); PRE uses the EW-universe book. Nifty 500 is a price index (no dividends).
* Absolute ranges use the DEV equal-weight drift (a strong small-cap period). The +5%/yr plan is round-2's haircut, not estimated here.
* 20-day excess and IC are nearly uncorrelated in DEV (corr 0.039); that is why C2 (AND) cuts false alarms so
  much. 20-60-day blocks cannot represent year-long joint slumps of money and signal, so C2's false alarm may be optimistic
  if such regimes exist. The IC is persistent only inside the label window (daily autocorr lag 1 0.85,
  lag 20 -0.008).
* 2026 money vs signal disagreement: IC 0.063 and relative hit 0.567 were
  normal, but the 13-week top-20 raw lead averaged -0.0% per 20 days (DEV 1.3%).
  The rules, by design, keep such a book running; the client must accept that.
* Variants: exposure 3 policies (+1 diagnostic) on 2 books x 3 periods; kill rules 3 pre-declared + 3 pre-justified combos. Selection on DEV only.
